What Is Net Revenue Retention (NRR)?

Explainerlowob research

By lowob · 17 November 2026 · 5-minute read · Revenue

In short: Net revenue retention (NRR) is the revenue a firm earns from a group of existing customers at the end of a period, divided by what the same customers paid at the start. It includes expansion, downgrades and churn, and excludes new customers. Above 100% means the existing base grows on its own. Its companion, gross revenue retention (GRR), excludes expansion and can never exceed 100%.

Key points

  • SaaS Capital calculates NRR as recurring revenue now from customers who were also customers a year ago, divided by total recurring revenue a year ago.
  • In SaaS Capital's 2025 survey, median NRR for private B2B SaaS companies with annual contracts of $25,000 to $50,000 was 102%, with a top quartile of 111%.
  • The 2024 KeyBanc Capital Markets and Sapphire Ventures survey of more than 100 private SaaS companies put net retention at about 101% and gross retention at about 90%.
  • Bessemer's 2021 analysis of cloud companies found average NRR of about 140% at $1 million to $10 million of ARR, falling to about 120% at larger scale.
  • NRR can hide churn: strong upsell in a few accounts can offset losses in many, which is why GRR should be reported beside it.

What net revenue retention means

NRR is a cohort measure. It fixes a group of customers at a start date and follows their revenue over a set period, usually 12 months. SaaS Capital's definition uses December to December: recurring revenue this December from customers who were also customers last December, divided by all recurring revenue last December. It includes upsells, cross-sells and price increases, so it can run well above 100%. GRR uses the same formula without upsells, cross-sells and price increases.

An illustrative cohort:

Movement over 12 monthsRevenue
Starting annual recurring revenue from the cohort£1,000,000
Expansion (upsell, cross-sell, price rises)+£150,000
Contraction (downgrades, fewer seats)−£40,000
Churn (customers who left)−£80,000
Ending revenue from the same customers£1,030,000
NRR103%
GRR (excludes expansion)88%

Revenue from customers won during the year is excluded from both. Including it is the most common way NRR gets overstated.

Why it matters for a commercial team

NRR shows how much of next year's growth the firm already has. At 110%, the existing base adds 10% before any new customer is signed. At 95%, sales must replace five points of lost revenue before growth begins. SaaS Capital found that companies with NRR of 110% or more grew faster than the 24% median for companies above $1 million of ARR, while those below 100% grew more slowly.

Benchmarks vary by sample and segment. Bessemer reported much higher averages than the private-company surveys, which partly reflects its sample of fast-growing cloud businesses. It also found smaller-contract businesses typically retain less: its examples included one company at 109% on contracts of about $2,000 and another at 123% on contracts above $50,000. SaaS Capital likewise reports that higher net retention correlates with higher contract values, and recommends benchmarking against firms of similar contract size rather than similar age or revenue.

Andreessen Horowitz makes the key caution in its startup metrics guide: gross churn "estimates the actual loss to the business, while net revenue churn understates the losses." A firm with 115% NRR and 75% GRR is losing a quarter of its starting revenue every year and buying it back through expansion. That is a different business from one with 105% NRR and 95% GRR.

In lowob's model, retention is an outcome to write back. Each renewal, expansion or loss should carry its reason in the commercial record, so the firm can see which decisions produced the number and not just the number itself.

How to measure it without flattering it

QuestionRecommended practiceWhy
Which customers are in the cohort?Only those billing at the start dateNew logos inflate NRR
What period?12 months, trailingMonthly figures are noisy and seasonal
Which revenue?Recurring revenue onlyOne-off services distort expansion
Price increases?Include, but report separatelyPrice-led NRR may not repeat
Report alone?Always with GRR and logo retentionNRR can mask broad churn

For firms without subscriptions, such as agencies or advisory practices, the equivalent is repeat revenue: what last year's clients paid this year, as a share of what they paid last year. The same exclusions apply.

Three checks catch the common errors. First, rebuild the cohort from billing data, not the CRM, since CRM close dates and invoice dates often differ. Second, split NRR by segment and contract size. Third, list the ten largest expansions and the ten largest losses, with reasons. If a handful of accounts produce most of the expansion, the headline figure is fragile.

lowob takeaways

  • NRR measures the base, not the funnel. New customers stay out of the calculation.
  • Report GRR beside it. Expansion can hide churn that would otherwise be obvious.
  • Benchmark by contract size. Smaller contracts retain less, so compare like with like.
  • Record the reasons. A renewal or loss with no reason attached cannot inform the next decision.

Common questions

How do you calculate net revenue retention?

Take recurring revenue now from customers who were customers a year ago, and divide it by total recurring revenue from those customers a year ago. Exclude revenue from new customers.

What is a good NRR?

The 2024 KeyBanc and Sapphire survey put private SaaS net retention at about 101%. SaaS Capital's 2025 median for $25,000 to $50,000 contracts was 102%, with a top quartile of 111%.

What is the difference between NRR and GRR?

NRR includes expansion such as upsells and price rises. GRR excludes expansion and counts only what was kept after downgrades and churn, so it cannot exceed 100%.

Is NRR the same as net dollar retention?

Yes. Net dollar retention (NDR) and net revenue retention are used interchangeably, though firms define the cohort and period differently, so check the definition.

Sources and notes

  • SaaS Capital, SaaS Retention Benchmarks for Private B2B Companies, September 2025. Lender's annual survey of private SaaS firms; definitions and medians used here.
  • Sapphire Ventures, KeyBanc Capital Markets and Sapphire Ventures Private SaaS Company Survey, October 2024. Press release on a survey of 100+ private SaaS companies.
  • Bessemer Venture Partners, Scaling to $100 Million, 2021. Venture firm analysis; sample skews to high-growth cloud companies.
  • Andreessen Horowitz, 16 Startup Metrics, August 2015, updated 2024. Investor guidance on gross versus net churn.

Next Move

Pull last year's customer list from billing, not the CRM, and calculate both NRR and GRR for that cohort. If the gap between them is more than 15 points, list the accounts that produced the expansion and ask whether it will repeat.
